# Driveline and wheel bearing noises

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Install a 24-spline involute companion flange onto the rear slip yoke. [t525]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove the rear slip yoke from the transfer case output.
2. [Partial] Install a companion flange designed for 24-spline involute splines onto the pinion or t-case output.

_Procedure reported by [t525]._

## Parts

- [Partial] Companion Flange: Must be 1310 series with 24 spline to fit Nissan style involute splines [t525]
- Driveshaft Yoke: Options include 1330, 1350, or 1410 depending on source vehicle, Frontier/Titan/Pathfinder [t525]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Nissan uses involute splines instead of standard cut; ensure the companion flange matches this spec. [t525]
